attempted_claim: Does there exist an integer residue r with gcd(r,30)=1 and an integer set H={h_1,...,h_28} with 0<=h_1<h_2<...<h_28<=1000 such that (i) every h_i is congruent to r modulo 30, and (ii) H is admissible, meaning for every prime p<=28 the residues {h_i mod p} omit at least one class modulo p? A complete answer is either the explicit r and list H together with, for each prime p<=28, an omitted residue class, or a complete proof that no 28-element subset of any coprime residue class modulo 30 inside an interval of length 1000 is admissible.
